column1: # One row per case, five tab-separated columns:
#   fixture   the envelope in this suite's fixtures/, or `-` for a run that must be
#             refused before either stand-in is reached
#   args      what this case adds to the invocation; a NAME=value word is put in the
#             run's environment instead, which is how a case reaches a stub's refusal
#   exit      the status the caller reads: 0 an answer, 2 a call this script cannot act on
#   expect    `|`-separated fragments the output must contain
#   note      what the case is here to hold

column5: an update landed mid-session: the tree to re-read is the installed one, not the loaded one
the predecessor is the highest version STRICTLY below the loaded one, never itself
versions rank by semver, not alphabetically (0.9.0 sorts above 0.10.0 as text)

column4: cache=absent|reload_needed=no|the loaded tree is ahead of what is installed|predecessor=unknown
column5: a working copy runs ahead of the registry: nothing to reload, nothing to diff against

column4: predecessor=unknown|no earlier version is left in the cache
column5: a swept predecessor is an ordinary answer, not a failure
the registry could not answer: fall back to the cache and say which source answered

column4: did not answer a JSON list|installed_source=cache
column5: output that is not a JSON list is a reason, not a parse that yields nothing
an unreachable forge never reads as agreement with what is installed
a source that is not a path in the marketplace repo falls back to the entry's own version
a marketplace no longer configured leaves upstream unknown, with the reason
a flag without its value is a call this script cannot act on, before any stand-in runs
an unknown flag stops rather than being read as a root
a directory holding no manifest is a caller's mistake, not an unknown version
